P	For centuries, it was just a pile of <b>Forge</b> <b>Lord</b> ruins (page 156) at the end of the <b>West Road</b> (page 270), up in the <b>Huffel</b> <b>Peaks</b> (page 236). A few generations back, ambitious folk started hauling ore out of the Delves. Foundry got built, merchants showed up, and coin flowed in—along with a constant trickle of folks seeking opportunity, or with nowhere else to go.
P	There's no town council, not even a militia to speak of. And unlike Stonetop, there ain't much sense of community. Some folks got friends, and allies, and reputations to lean on. But when it comes right down to it, sure seems like everyone's only looking out for themselves.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	When was the last round of violence between the Delvers and the Hillfolk? What did it cost you, personally?
Q	Which of you have been here before? When? Why?
Q	Who up here should you never, ever cross?
Q	Who's the merchant who trades with Stonetop the most?
Q	Who left Stonetop to come up here? What's the last you've heard of them?
Q	What are they said to eat up here, besides goats and imported grain?
Q	According to the stories you've heard, who the hell was Gordin?

H2	Places
HR
B	<b>The slopes near town</b>, all sludge and mud and tree stumps, mining camps and goat herds
B	<b>Sorrow's Gate</b>, where the West Road ends, a sprawl of tents, no permanent structures on the pave stones
B	<b>The Arms</b>, two ridges that cradle the town, Maker-ruins clinging to their sides
B	<b>Foundry</b>, a brick slab squatted at the town's foot, belching smoke and slurry
B	<b>The ancient aqueduct</b>, still in use, feeding Foundry and turning its waterwheel
B	<b>The Terraces</b>, seven of them, crowded with shops, stables, tenements, alleys, and people. Make-do construction lashed to humbling ruins
B	<b>The Swap</b>, an open-air market for labor, second-hand goods, questionable food or pleasures, and the odd Delve-finds
B	<b>A half-dozen walled-off compounds</b>, claiming the best spots, built into Maker-ruins
B	<b>The three Delves</b>, gaping tunnels into the dark, miners coming and going
H2	People
P	No one is from here originally. Even folks born here, their parents or grandparents came from somewhere else. For any NPC, pick or roll where they're from and what brought them. Pick a name based on their origins, maybe with an epithet like "the Knife," "Gaptooth," "Limper," "Boils," "the Yellow," or "Go-Between."

ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Bosses</b> each run big parts of the local economy; everyone in town relies on what they control. Their positions are far from stable, and when one topples, there's turmoil. Each is attended by 10-15 family, servants, and retainers.
B2	Mutra the Teeth (mines, timber)
B2	Odo Thriceborn (mines, housing)
B2	Honest Draigh (trade with Marshedge, food)
B2	Jahalim of the Keys (Foundry)
B2	Smiling Ffransis (water, booze)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Merchants</b> bring goods and raw material in and out of Gordin's Delve. Most are backed by one of the Bosses, but one or two manage the careful dance of independence. (~10 operations, or ~25 souls total)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The Keeps</b> keep the town running, such that it does. They run the trades, the shops, the inns, the boarding houses, the hostelries, the dens of vice. They don't mine the Delves, they mine the miners. And the Bosses mine <i>them</i>. (~50 souls, including family and apprentices)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Miners</b> make up the bulk of the town. Small crews work what claims they can, usually veins far down the Delves or dotting the slopes. They'll be gone for days on end. The Bosses' crews are bigger, working the best veins on day/night shifts. It's hard work, that barely pays enough to get by. (~250 souls)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Prospectors</b> work alone or in small teams, seeking new claims and selling them to mining crews. They also sell Maker artifacts to the Bosses when they can, or else at the Swap for whatever they can get. Prospecting is terribly dangerous, but a way to make good coin fast. (~5-10 souls at any given time)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Smelters</b> work at Foundry, processing raw ore into iron, copper, silver, lead, and tin. There's a handful of skilled smiths, too, but mostly it's hard, hot, dangerous work. Pay's decent, though, and you don't have to go down the Delves. (~50 souls, working in shifts)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Loggers</b> ply the mountainsides for timber and haul it back to town, for construction or to fuel hearths and Foundry's furnace. The nearby slopes were stripped clean long ago, so nowadays loggers range farther out into the mountains. Hard, dangerous work that takes folks away from town for weeks at a time. (~50 souls)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>The desperate</b> can't find work or can't keep it, due to injury, infirmity, or temperament. They take what gigs they can, or they scavenge, or they die slowly out near Sorrow's Gate. Some turn to robbery and theft, but unless they're very good, they're beaten or killed by victims, mobs, or other cutthroats. And if you are very good at thuggery? Well, the Bosses probably have work for you. (~100-200 souls, always in flux)
ICON	icons/people.svg
B	<b>Beyond that</b>, another ~100-150 souls do odd jobs: goat herding, butchering, hauling water, cleaning and cooking, working for the Keeps or the Bosses as staff or muscle or entertainment or a combination of all three. They often live with their employers, or their stock.
P	There are very few full-time homemakers in Gordin's Delve; almost everybody works or hustles a little. Even kids are put to work as soon as possible. It's not a nice place, not at all.

H2	Secrets
HR
B	<b>The Red Door</b> is a well-known feature down in the <b>First Delve</b> (page 198), a 20-foot tall slab of <b>makerglass</b> (page 388), inlaid with hundreds of patterned tiles. Some are missing, allowing the tiles to be slid around. When the tiles are in the exact right spots, the Red Door will open. Hints to the correct arrangement are hidden in old mosaics throughout Gordin's Delve.
B	<b>An established shopkeep</b> (like a chandler, a publican, an innkeeper, maybe even a barber?) has a habit of killing folks who won't be missed. They're otherwise a pillar of the community.
B	Everyone knows there are <b>grates in the</b> <b>terraces</b>, carrying water through chutes and culverts to pour out below Sorrow's Gate. But there's more, a series of cramped tunnels and chutes that connect to some of the old ruins and even the Delves. The sewers are gross, infested with rats or worse, and just big enough to get lost in.
B	<b>A cult of locals</b> (some influential) have taken to tossing sacrifices into the underground lake at the bottom of the <b>Second Delve</b> (page 198): coin, flesh, living victims. They've received blessings from <b>Daagon</b> (page 419) as a result.
B	Every few years, miners in the <b>Third Delve</b> (page 198) will unearth a "door" made of <b>orichalcum</b> (page 162). Rarely, they rebury it.
P	Usually, they pry it open, to find nothing but more rock beyond. A powerful earthquake always follows a few days after one of these doors is opened, but few have made the connection.
H2	Hooks
B	The PCs' favorite merchant is in trouble with one or more Bosses
B	An ambitious Keep is angling to become a new Boss
B	Miners, smelters, and loggers seek to organize and throw off the Bosses' yoke
B	A small mining crew has gone missing; a worried loved one asks for help
B	One of the Bosses was just killed by an underling, who's desperately trying to assume their position
B	Ustrina offer gold and silver for something unsavory (fresh blood, corpses, slaves, etc.)
B	Logging crews have gone missing, and the folks who went to check on them never came back. Are Hillfolk raiders to blame? Bandits? Or something worse?

H3	Shoddy construction
P	Gordin's Delve is a weird mix of piled stone and crude carpentry, lashed onto Maker-ruins that have stood for hundreds of years. It's all very slapdash and precarious.
P	• Things creak, sway, and teeter ominously
P	• A wall/support/floor gives way, putting someone in danger
P	• Someone falls from a height/is buried under rubble
P	• Something catches fire
P	• A structure collapses, weakening others
P	• A home/shop is destroyed, someone's savings/livelihood/family is lost
PAGE	198
H2	The Delves
HR
P	The Arms feature three archways, each over 30 feet tall. Each arch leads to a tunnel of smooth stone that plunges into the mountain, eventually connecting to the <b>Labyrinth</b> (page 242). Side passages, chambers, and complexes branch off the main tunnels—some ancient, some excavated in the last 50 years.
P	<b>The First Delve</b> opens where the two Arms meet. It stretches half a mile from the surface, then becomes a series of switchback tunnels, one after the other, down and down and down. The main tunnel ends with a cave-in, but side passages and chambers connect to the Labyrinth.
P	<b>Forge Lord</b> carvings (page 156) decorate the walls, and rich veins of copper and hematite (iron ore) have been found.
P	<b>The Second Delve</b> opens on the righthand slope (facing uphill). The delve goes straight, sloping down for about 300 feet, then turns left at a landing. Another 300 feet, there's another landing, another left turn. The pattern repeats dozens of times, ending at a ledge that overlooks a subterranean lake. Miners brick up the end of the passage, but their walls rarely stand for long. Ancient side passages spoke outward from this delve; many have led to rich (though inconvenient) copper veins.
B	<b>The Third Delve</b> opens on the lefthand Arm. The main tunnel forks and turns frequently, soon becoming one great big twisting mess of tunnels and chambers. Many of these lower tunnels connect with the Labyrinth. Hematite veins have been found at the end of many such tunnels, and turned into active mines.

H3	Impressions
B	Vast, arched tunnels, stretching well beyond your torchlight
B	Echoing sounds of picks on rock, carts rumbling, voices grumbling, your own footsteps
B	That sense of immense, merciless weight above you
B	A smooth, rippling texture to the main tunnel walls, less like they were carved and more like they were… melted?
B	Constant, warm breeze flowing up, like gentle breath
B	Crude, cramped scale of new excavations, propped up with timbers
